```{r read data, include=FALSE}

data <- read.csv("data/main_data.csv")

# slice top 2 rows of redundant info

data <- data %>%
  slice(-(1:2))

# apply exclusion criteria (exclude pps who complete in under half the median time)

data$Duration..in.seconds. <- as.numeric(data$Duration..in.seconds.)

cutoff <- median(data$Duration..in.seconds., na.rm = TRUE) / 2

# median is 635.5 seconds, half is 317.75 = 27 exclusions (2.7% of sample)

data <- data %>%
  filter(Duration..in.seconds. > cutoff)

#add row number identifier

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(id = row_number()) %>%
  dplyr::select(id, everything())

```

```{r create functions, include=FALSE}

# converting classic likert scale to numeric 

likert_numeric <- function(response) {
  
  # Trim leading and trailing whitespace and convert to lowercase
  response_cleaned <- tolower(trimws(response))
  
  # Define the mapping with all lowercase keys
  mapping <- c(
    "strongly disagree" = 1,
    "disagree" = 2,
    "somewhat disagree" = 3,
    "neither agree nor disagree" = 4,
    "somewhat agree" = 5,
    "agree" = 6,
    "strongly agree" = 7
  )
  
  # Return the mapped value, or NA if the response does not match
  return(ifelse(!is.na(mapping[response_cleaned]), mapping[response_cleaned], NA))
  
  # convert to numeric
  return(as.numeric(numeric_values))
}

# convert to 0, 1 factor

make_factor <- function(data, cols) {
  data %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        all_of(cols),
        ~ factor(.x, levels = c("0", "1"))
      )
    )
}

# set factor levels for ideology variables

level_ideology <- function(data, vars) {
  ideology_levels <- c(
    "Strongly left-leaning",
    "Left-leaning",
    "Somewhat left-leaning",
    "Neither left nor right leaning",
    "Somewhat right-leaning",
    "Right-leaning",
    "Strongly right-leaning"
  )
  
  data %>%
    mutate(across(
      all_of(vars),
      ~ factor(.x, levels = ideology_levels, ordered = TRUE)
    ))
}

# set factor levels for individual categorical variables

# Convert multiple character vars to factors with specified level orders
# - levels_map: named list with all pre-specific vectors
# - ordered_cols: character vector of column names that should be ordered factors
# - append_unknown: if TRUE, unseen values in the data are appended to the end of levels
# - warn_unknown: if TRUE, warn about unseen values
set_factor_levels <- function(data, levels_map, ordered_cols = character(),
                              append_unknown = TRUE, warn_unknown = TRUE) {

  stopifnot(is.list(levels_map), !is.null(names(levels_map)))
  cols <- intersect(names(levels_map), names(data))
  if (length(cols) == 0) return(data)

  data %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(cols), ~ {
      lvls <- levels_map[[cur_column()]]
      x <- .x

      # Handle values not in the provided levels
      if (append_unknown) {
        miss <- setdiff(unique(x), lvls)
        if (warn_unknown && length(miss) > 0) {
          warning(sprintf(
            "Column '%s': appending %d unknown level(s): %s",
            cur_column(), length(miss), paste(miss, collapse = ", ")
          ))
        }
        lvls <- c(lvls, setdiff(miss, lvls))
      } else {
        miss <- setdiff(unique(x), lvls)
        if (warn_unknown && length(miss) > 0) {
          warning(sprintf(
            "Column '%s': %d value(s) not in provided levels will become NA: %s",
            cur_column(), length(miss), paste(miss, collapse = ", ")
          ))
        }
      }

      factor(x, levels = lvls, ordered = cur_column() %in% ordered_cols)
    }))
}

# Mean-score items

mean_score <- function(data, vars, new_name) {
  data %>%
    mutate(
      !!new_name := rowMeans(across(all_of(vars)), na.rm = TRUE)
    )
}

```

### Sample

```{r sample wrangle, include=FALSE}

# extract ideology of self and perceived party ideology, and demographics

sample <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(id, starts_with("trial"), contains("ideology"), region, education, age, gender, ethnicity, interest, law)

# set levels for ideology

sample <- level_ideology(
  sample,
  vars = c("self_ideology", "alliance_ideology", "sdp_ideology")
)

# set mapping levels for all other variables

region <- c("England", "Scotland", "Wales", "Northern Ireland")
education <- c("No formal qualifications", "O levels/GCSEs or equivalent", "A levels or equivalent", "Foundation degree or equivalent", "Undergraduate degree or equivalent", "Postgraduate degree (e.g., Masters, PhD) or equivalent", "Other, please describe")
gender <- c("Female", "Male", "Non-binary / third gender", "Prefer not to say")
ethnicity <- c("White", "Asian", "Black", "Mixed/Multiple ethnic groups", "Arab", "Other, please describe", "Prefer not to say")
interest <- c("Not at all interested", "Somewhat interested", "Interested", "Very interested")

# create list to be inputted to function

levels_map <- list(
  region = region,
  education = education,
  gender = gender,
  ethnicity = ethnicity,
  interest = interest
)

# apply previously created function

sample <- set_factor_levels(
  sample,
  levels_map = levels_map,
  ordered_cols = c("education", "interest", "self_ideology"),
  append_unknown = TRUE,   
  warn_unknown = TRUE
)

# Check correct application
lapply(sample[names(levels_map)], levels)

# age to numeric

sample$age <- as.numeric(sample$age)
summary(sample$age)

```

#### What was the demographic breakdown of the sample?

```{r table, include=FALSE}

# function to create demographic breakdown table
demographic_table <- function(data, vars, total_n) {
  bind_rows(lapply(vars, function(v) {
    data %>%
      count(!!sym(v), name = "N") %>%
      mutate(
        Variable = v,
        Level = as.character(!!sym(v)),
        Percent = round(100 * N / total_n, 1)
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(Variable, Level, N, Percent)
  })) %>%
    arrange(match(Variable, vars)) %>%
    mutate(
      Percent = paste0(Percent, "%")
    )
}

# specify variables in the order you want them
vars <- c("region", "gender", "education", "ethnicity", "self_ideology", "interest")

# create table
sample_table <- demographic_table(sample, vars, total_n = 985)

# pretty print
kable(sample_table, align = c("l","l","r","r"),
      col.names = c("Variable", "Category", "N", "%"))

```

```{r echo=FALSE}

display_names <- c(
  region         = "Region",
  gender         = "Gender",
  education      = "Education",
  ethnicity      = "Ethnicity",
  self_ideology  = "Self-identified ideology",
  interest       = "Political interest"
)

# 1) Prepare columns (rename, parse Percent, keep current row order)
sample_table2 <- sample_table %>%
  mutate(.row_order = row_number()) %>%                       # preserve within-block order
  rename(Category = Level) %>%
  mutate(
    Percent = as.numeric(gsub("%", "", Percent)) / 100        # "45.4%" -> 0.454
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable_display = recode(Variable, !!!display_names),    # <-- creates Variable_display
    Variable_display = factor(Variable_display, levels = block_order)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Variable_display, .row_order)

# set order of presentation

block_order <- c(
  "Region",
  "Gender",
  "Education",
  "Ethnicity",
  "Self-identified ideology",
  "Political interest"
)

# 3) Build table
sample_table2 %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable_display, Category, N, Percent) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Variable_display") %>%
  cols_label(
    Category = "Category",
    N        = "N",
    Percent  = "% of sample"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = N, decimals = 0) %>%
  fmt_percent(columns = Percent, decimals = 1) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(13),
    data_row.padding = px(4)
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_row_groups()
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(source_note = "Totals are out of N = 985.")
```

```{r wide to long}

# repeated measures final column names

r_measures <- c(
  "skill","princ","emp","know","sinc","kind","comp","truth","warm",
  "agree1","agree2","proact","look","intent","open","use","compliant",
  "policy","ideology","support","familiar"
)

# 1) Make the two-row-per-id trial table 
trial_long <- data %>%
  select(id, vote, self_ideology, matches("^trial(1|2)_(party|motive|imprint|label)$")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^trial(1|2)_(party|motive|imprint|label)$"),
    names_to = c("trial", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "^trial(1|2)_(.*)$"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    trial = as.integer(trial),
    party = as.integer(party),
    motive = as.integer(motive),
    imprint = as.integer(imprint)
  )

# 2) Prepare party-specific data for alliance (a_/alliance_) and sdp (s_/sdp_)

# Make alliance-by-id by stripping prefixes and adding _A suffix
alliance_by_id <- data %>%
  select(id, starts_with("a_"), starts_with("alliance_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("^a_", "", .x),           starts_with("a_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("^alliance_", "", .x),    starts_with("alliance_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ ifelse(.x == "id", .x, paste0(.x, "_A")))

# Make sdp-by-id with _S suffix
sdp_by_id <- data %>%
  select(id, starts_with("s_"), starts_with("sdp_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("^s_",   "", .x), starts_with("s_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("^sdp_", "", .x), starts_with("sdp_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ ifelse(.x == "id", .x, paste0(.x, "_S")))

# 4) Join both party blocks onto the trial table
long_data <- trial_long %>%
  left_join(alliance_by_id, by = "id") %>%
  left_join(sdp_by_id,      by = "id") %>%
  mutate(
    !!!set_names(
      lapply(r_measures, function(m) {
        a <- sym(paste0(m, "_A"))
        s <- sym(paste0(m, "_S"))
        # build an expression that will be evaluated in the data mask
        expr(if_else(.data$party == 0L, !!a, !!s))
      }),
      r_measures
    )
  ) %>%
  select(id, trial, party, motive, imprint, label, all_of(r_measures), vote, self_ideology) %>%
  arrange(id, trial)


```

```{r final variable transformations}

# semantic differentials

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(across(
    c(skill, princ, emp, know, sinc, comp, kind, warm, truth),
    strip_to_numeric
  ))

# vote

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(
    vote = case_when(
      vote == "The Alliance Party of Northern Ireland" ~ 0,
      vote == "The Social Democratic Party (SDP)" ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

# manipulations

long_data <- make_factor(long_data, c("party", "imprint", "motive", "vote"))

# familiarity

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(
    familiar = case_when(
      familiar == "Yes, I have heard of them"      ~ "1",
      familiar == "No, I do not know who they are" ~ "0",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    familiar = factor(familiar, levels = c("0", "1"))
  )

# support

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(
    support = case_when(
      support == "Strongly oppose"    ~ 1,
      support == "Oppose"             ~ 2,
      support == "Somewhat oppose"    ~ 3,
      support == "No opinion"         ~ 4,
      support == "Somewhat support"   ~ 5,
      support == "Support"            ~ 6,
      support == "Strongly support"   ~ 7,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

# create trustworthiness dimensions

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mean_score(vars = c("skill", "know", "comp"), new_name = "competence") %>%
  mean_score(vars = c("princ", "sinc", "truth"), new_name = "integrity") %>%
  mean_score(vars = c("emp", "kind", "warm"), new_name = "benevolence")

```

## Hypothesis testing

```{r decomposing covariates}



```

H1. Participants informed that a political party engages in intentional information disclosure will report higher perceptions of trustworthiness (across all dimensions) compared to those informed a party only shares what is necessary.

H3. Intentionality will moderate the effect of viewing an advertising disclosure on perceived trustworthiness (across all dimensions), such that a disclosure will increase trustworthiness only when the political party is known to share information intentionally.

```{r H1}

# Basic preregistered model
m1 <- lmer(competence ~ motive*imprint + party + (1 | id),
           data = long_data, REML = FALSE)

summary(m1)

```

H4. Intentionality will increase the likelihood of voting for a political party, and this effect will be mediated by perceptions of trustworthiness (all dimensions)

```{r causal mediation}

# 0) Build a common analysis dataset (same rows for both models)
med.dat <- long_data %>%
  dplyr::select(id, vote, motive, imprint, party, competence) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na() %>%                 # ensure identical row set
  mutate(
    id      = as.factor(id),           
    vote    = as.numeric(vote)         # 0/1 numeric for glmer
  ) %>%
  mutate(vote = vote - 1)

## 1) Mediator model (random intercept)
med.fit <- nlme::lme(
  fixed   = competence ~ motive + imprint + party,
  random  = ~ 1 | id,
  data    = med.dat,
  na.action = na.omit
)

med.fit <- lmer(
  competence ~ motive + imprint + party + (1 | id),
  data = med.dat
)

# 2) Outcome model as GLM (logit) — no random effect
out.fit <- glm(
  vote ~ motive + competence + imprint + party,
  data   = med.dat,
  family = binomial("logit")
)

## 3) Mediation (ACME/ADE/Total; bootstrap CIs recommended)
med.out <- mediate(
  model.m   = med.fit,
  model.y   = out.fit,
  treat     = "motive",
  mediator  = "competence",
  boot      = FALSE,
  cluster = med.dat$id,
  sims      = 1000
)


# no cluster within med and out models

med.fit <- lm(competence ~ motive + imprint + party, data = med.dat)


```
